chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarmi, he said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام: Is sajdah on linen and cotton permissible without taqiyyah? He said: It is permissible.

So the meaning in this report is that sajdah on these two materials is permissible when there is no taqiyyah, on condition that another necessity arises, such as heat or cold and what is similar to them. And he did not say that this is permissible without taqiyyah or anything that takes its place; that indicates this.

key_terms.الْقُطْنِ: cotton as a material on which sajdah is discussed
key_terms.الْكَتَّانِ: linen as a material on which sajdah is discussed
key_terms.بَرْدٍ: cold as an example of necessity
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: dissimulation or precaution due to danger or sensitive circumstances
key_terms.حَرٍّ: heat as an example of necessity
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٌ: a necessity that justifies an exception

ai.seo_question: Is sajdah on cotton and linen permissible without taqiyyah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of performing sajdah on cotton and linen. Although the Imam عليه السلام says it is permissible, the closing clarification explains that this permissibility is understood in cases of necessity, such as heat or cold, or circumstances comparable to taqiyyah.
